title: Growth strategy options and execution plays

gates.text: Evidence: every forecast number has a cited source and grade or is labelled 'assumption, grade D'; no invented statistics, customers or results.

Execution portfolio: limit costed plays to the confirmed budget, capacity, evidence and permission gates. Separately preserve grounded, adjacent and bold strategy options; do not require a precedent, high predictability, immediate feasibility or budget share to generate/display a bold option. Keep novelty, evidence, fit, feasibility and risk separate.
Compliance: no bought or gated reviews, review incentives on Google, undisclosed endorsements, SMS without consent, astroturfing or platform-violating tactics.

anchors.1: Channels without a named audience, place or hook ('post on Instagram', 'run ads').
anchors.3: Audiences and hooks named for most plays, but some are generic or unverified.
anchors.5: Every play names who and where (with size when known), the trigger, the exact hook and the asset only this business has.

anchors.1: The swap test passes: any competitor could run this plan unchanged; mostly social and email.
anchors.3: One play is a transplant or non-obvious channel; the rest are standard.
anchors.5: Distinct mechanisms grounded in this business’s assets or explicit hypotheses, with a concrete buyer benefit and reversible test. Originality does not require an existing precedent.

anchors.1: Invents forecasts, promises results, hides uncertainty, or omits the next useful measurement.
anchors.3: Outcomes are conditional or honestly unknown, but the measurement chain, evidence or decision consequence is incomplete.
anchors.5: Supplied inputs support a transparent funnel and conditional scenarios; missing inputs remain unknown with a concrete collection plan and decision rule. No forecast is required when evidence cannot support it. Evidence strength and largest uncertainty are explicit.

anchors.3: Tests named but sizes, budgets or kill rules missing.
anchors.5: Every play has a bounded test, feasible duration, time and cash cap, useful observation and stop/change/continue rules. Statistical sample sizes are justified only when base rates and design permit; otherwise a clearly limited observational or qualitative test is appropriate.

anchors.1: Ignores budget, owner hours or unit economics.
anchors.3: Fits the budget but not checked against margin or capacity.
anchors.5: Fits confirmed cash and time constraints; planned effort is nonzero for manual work and gated when availability is unknown. Uses deterministic economics when supported; otherwise states missing value, margin or retention and prevents unjustified scaling. Names how success could compound.

anchors.3: Clear steps but no first action.
anchors.5: Each play ends with a first action under 30 minutes and what ClimbOS will do for the owner.

anchors.1: A list of channels or arbitrary volume targets without a distinctive business direction.
anchors.3: A direction and a bounded test, but the compounding mechanism or path to the next horizon is weak.
anchors.5: A precise buyer and business ambition, a distinctive mechanism and compounding advantage, deliberate trade-offs, a credible current bet and next horizon. Unknown scale remains unknown; a validation-first move is strong when it resolves the binding uncertainty. Speculative bold choices remain visible without fabricated forecasts.

anchors.1: Hooks pull no lever (no bigger outcome, confidence, speed or ease); comparison pages list features with no named alternative or best-fit segment; referral asks have no trigger.
anchors.3: Some hooks name a lever and some pages name the alternative, but the best-fit segment or the share moment is vague.
anchors.5: Every hook names the lever it pulls in the customer's words; comparison pages lead with one strength for a named segment against a named alternative; referral plays have a trigger and a built-in share moment; self-serve products get a funnel play.

anchors.1: No grounded, adjacent and bold options, or bold is omitted because it lacks precedent or has low feasibility.
anchors.3: Three options appear but are only weakly distinct, weakly tied to the business, or the bold test is vague.
anchors.5: Grounded, adjacent and genuinely original bold choices are distinct; uncertainty and upside are clear; the test is reversible and decision-relevant.
